def parse(
    text: T.Optional[str],
    style: T.Union[DocstringStyle, str, BaseParser] = DocstringStyle.AUTO,
    sections: T.Optional[T.Sequence[SectionSpec]] = None,
) -> Docstring:
    """Parse the docstring into its components.

    :param text: docstring text to parse
    :param style: the style's name, such as ``"google"`` or
        ``DocstringStyle.GOOGLE``, or a parser to parse with
    :param sections: the sections, or fields, to recognise instead of the
        style's own, as described in :mod:`docstring_parser.sections`; in
        auto mode, every style recognises them. A parser has its own.
    :returns: parsed docstring representation
    """
    if isinstance(style, BaseParser):
        if sections is not None:
            raise ValueError("A parser has its sections; pass none")
        return style.parse(text)
    if not isinstance(style, DocstringStyle):
        style = DocstringStyle(style)
    if style != DocstringStyle.AUTO:
        return _parse_in(_STYLE_MAP[style], text, sections)
    if sections is None:
        return auto.detect(
            text, [module.parse for module in _STYLE_MAP.values()], True
        )
    return _auto_parsers.get(list(sections), auto.Parser, sections).parse(text)

    """Docstring object representation."""

    def __init__(
        self,
        style=None,  # type: T.Optional[DocstringStyle]

        self.short_description = None  # type: T.Optional[str]
        self.long_description = None  # type: T.Optional[str]
        self.blank_after_short_description = False
        self.blank_after_long_description = False
        self.meta = []  # type: T.List[DocstringMeta]
        self.style = style  # type: T.Optional[DocstringStyle]

    def __repr__(self) -> str:
        return _repr(
            self,
            (
                "style",
                "short_description",
                "long_description",
                "blank_after_short_description",
                "blank_after_long_description",
                "meta",
            ),
        )

    @property
    def description(self) -> T.Optional[str]:
        """Return the full description of the function

        Returns None if the docstring did not include any description
        """
        ret = []
        if self.short_description:
            ret.append(self.short_description)
            if self.blank_after_short_description:
                ret.append("")
        if self.long_description:
            ret.append(self.long_description)

        if not ret:
            return None

        return "\n".join(ret)

    @property
    def params(self) -> T.List[DocstringParam]:
        """Return a list of information on function params, without the
        attributes."""
        return [
            item
            for item in self.meta
            if isinstance(item, DocstringParam)
            and item.kind is not Kind.ATTRIBUTE
        ]

    @property
    def attrs(self) -> T.List[DocstringParam]:
        """Return a list of information on attributes."""
        return [

            for item in self.meta

        ]

    def params_by_name(self) -> T.Mapping[str, DocstringParam]:
        """Return the params by name, read-only.

        A name given twice maps to its first param; :attr:`params` keeps
        every one. Each access builds the mapping anew from :attr:`meta`.
        """
        return _by_name((item.arg_name, item) for item in self.params)

        """Return the attributes by name, read-only.

    "source": "class BaseParser:
    """A parser of one docstring style, set up with the sections to know.

    Build one once and call :meth:`parse` for every docstring; its sections
    are read when it is made, not on every call.
    """

    #: The name of the style the parser reads, such as ``"google"``.
    name: str

    def parse(self, text: T.Optional[str]) -> Docstring:
        """Parse a docstring into its components.

        :raises ParseError: for everything that could not be parsed
        """
        result = self.try_parse(text)
        if result.problems:
            raise parse_error(result)
        return result.docstring

    def try_parse(self, text: T.Optional[str]) -> ParseResult:
        """Parse what can be parsed of a docstring, and tell what cannot.

        Text that cannot be parsed goes to the long description.
